title: Sort by identity code
summary: Read the code of each item that the vision sensor sees and swing a diverter arm so that code 2 items leave on the side belt.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety.
objectives: Route items by an integer code instead of a switch.
Time an actuator against the travel of an item that has already been read.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/VisionSorting.st, run both belts after Start. Twelve items arrive one at a time, each with a code: every code 1 item must end in Product1 and every code 2 item in Product2, so the arm must be across the belt when a code 2 item reaches it and at rest when a code 1 item does. Done must light after twelve items.
stages.checkpoint: Code 1 items end in Product1, code 2 items in Product2, and Done lights after twelve items.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, work out when the arm must be across the belt: the code is read about two seconds before the item reaches the arm, and the arm takes a moment to swing. What happens to a code 2 item if the arm is not across when it arrives, and to a code 1 item if it is?
stages.checkpoint: The code is on Code for about a second and the item reaches the arm about two seconds after it is read: a code 2 item must find the arm across, and a code 1 item must find it at rest.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Write the program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no item is sorted. After Start both belts must run and each item must end in the bin of its code.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson, with the plant answering your outputs, and lists every assertion that failed. To watch the machine move, press {{ui:toolbar.run.label}} (F5) and open the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}}.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named vision-sorting and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Watch the {{ui:plant.panel.view3d}} and the vision readout: the code shows while the item is in the field, and a code 2 item slides onto the side belt in front of the arm.
stages.checkpoint: The arm is across the belt when each code 2 item reaches it, and at rest when each code 1 item does.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: The grade sees the two product belts and that nothing was dropped; it cannot see your timing, so a wrong timing shows only as an item in the wrong bin.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: The code is on the input for only about a second, and the same item is in the field for many scans, but the arm is further down the belt: what must your program remember about an item it has read, and for how long?

Latch Start into Active and run RunIn and RunSide while Active. Count scans of 0.01 s with three INT variables, Lock, Wait and ArmHold, each counted down by one per scan while above 0. When Active is TRUE, Lock = 0 and Code <> 0, add one to Handled, set Lock to 450 so the item is counted once, and if Code = 2 set Wait to 70. When Wait comes down to 0, set Divert and load ArmHold with 530, so a code 2 item read while the arm is still across renews the hold; when ArmHold comes down to 0, clear Divert. Done := Handled >= 12; Busy := Active AND NOT Done.

faultCases: The starting program drives no output, so no belt moves and no item is sorted.
